skill.name: cargo-content
skill.description: Manage the knowledge a Cargo workspace holds — upload files (PDF, CSV, text), rename and organize them, and build native or connector-backed libraries that sync from an external source, so agents can retrieve them (RAG). Triggers: "upload this PDF", "add these docs as knowledge", "build a knowledge base", "sync our help center into Cargo", "what files are in the workspace", "index this folder", "attach our pricing sheet". Skip when: wiring the file or library into an agent — use cargo-ai; uploading a CSV that drives a batch run — that is a workspace-management file upload.
skill.summary: Manage Cargo knowledge files and libraries for agent retrieval using the Cargo CLI.
skill.author: getcargohq

security_audit.summary: All 61 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, documentation links, Cargo resource identifiers, or legitimate workspace checks. No evidence found of prompt injection, unauthorized data transfer, or malicious execution in the reviewed files. The documented workflows require authenticated Cargo access and can upload, modify, or remove workspace content.

content.user_title: Manage Cargo Knowledge Files and Libraries
content.value_statement: Scattered documents make workspace knowledge difficult to maintain. This skill guides Cargo CLI workflows to upload, organize, and manage knowledge files and connector-backed libraries.
actual_capabilities: List and inspect Cargo knowledge files, including names, content types, sizes, and indexing indicators.
Upload PDF, CSV, and text files to a Cargo workspace, optionally selecting a destination folder.
Rename, move, and remove uploaded knowledge files using their Cargo identifiers.
List and inspect native or connector-backed libraries, with filters for library kind and connector.
Create connector-backed libraries using an existing connector, extractor, folder, and configuration.
Update library names, remove libraries, and reference the documented upload, attachment, and deployment sequence.
limitations: Requires the Cargo CLI, authenticated workspace access, and CLI version 1.0.19 or later for the documented content commands.
Folder creation, connector setup, and agent release management belong to related skills.
Uploading a file does not automatically attach it to an agent or guarantee retrieval readiness.
The exact library response envelope is not specified; connector configuration depends on the selected extractor.

use_cases.title: Maintain Product Knowledge
use_cases.description: Upload approved product documents, rename outdated labels, and organize files for later attachment to a support agent.

use_cases.title: Connect a Help Center
use_cases.description: Create a knowledge library from an existing help-center connector and inspect the resulting library details.

use_cases.title: Review Workspace Content
use_cases.description: Inspect file sizes, content types, and indexing indicators before planning agent knowledge updates.

prompt_templates.title: List Knowledge Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the active Cargo workspace, then list knowledge files with names, sizes, content types, and indexing indicators. Make no changes.

prompt_templates.title: Upload an Approved Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm my Cargo workspace, then upload ./product-docs.pdf as knowledge. Report the returned file identifier and explain whether agent attachment is still required.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Existing Files
prompt_templates.prompt: List Cargo files and folders, then propose moving selected research documents into the Research folder. Ask for confirmation before changing names or locations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: organize files using related folder-management guidance

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Connector Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Cargo connector-backed library named Help Center. Request missing connector, extractor, folder, and configuration details; show the plan before creating anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: configure an external knowledge source

output_examples.input: List my Cargo knowledge files without changing anything.
output: Illustrative result: knowledge-base.pdf is a PDF file with a size of 1 MB.
Its indexing indicator is enabled, and no folder is assigned.

output_examples.input: Why does my agent not use the library I created?
output: Creating a library does not automatically attach it to an agent.
Add the library to the agent draft release resources, then deploy the release using the related agent-management workflow.
Check file indexing indicators before expecting document retrieval.

output_examples.input: Prepare a connector-backed Help Center library.
output: The proposed library name is Help Center.
Provide the connector identifier, extractor slug, destination folder identifier, and extractor configuration.
Library creation will wait for those details and your confirmation.

best_practices: Confirm the active Cargo workspace and resource identifiers before uploading or modifying content.
Upload only documents approved for the workspace, and confirm removal or deployment actions before execution.
Inspect command responses and indexing indicators; use command help when connector configuration or response fields are unclear.
anti_patterns: Assuming an uploaded document is automatically available to every agent.
Using content uploads for batch-run input CSVs instead of the separate workspace-management upload surface.
Guessing connector, folder, or file identifiers instead of discovering the correct workspace resources.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It guides Cargo knowledge-file and library workflows, including uploads, inspection, organization, updates, and removal.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install the Cargo CLI, authenticate, and confirm the active workspace. The documented content commands require CLI version 1.0.19 or later.

faq.question: Which file formats are documented?
faq.answer: The examples cover PDFs, CSVs, and plain text. Other common document formats are mentioned, but no complete format list is provided.

faq.question: Does uploading a file make an agent use it?
faq.answer: No. Attach the file or library to the agent draft release resources and deploy that release through the related agent-management workflow.

faq.question: How do native and connector libraries differ?
faq.answer: Native libraries hold workspace-managed uploaded files. Connector libraries sync external documents through an existing connector and an unstructured-data extractor.

faq.question: Does the audit cover the Cargo service and installed CLI?
faq.answer: No. This audit reviews the supplied skill documents, not the installed npm package, Cargo service, connector permissions, or workspace data.
